body:
claude-storymodel4s critique of the Narrative Atlas proposal rev 0 (docs/plans/2026-08-28-narrative-atlas-proposal.md), grounded in M0 types. Verdict first: the governing idea (one identity system, several typed projections with declared contracts; scene compiler with laws; epistemic playhead) is right and is the only design consistent with mission §Boundaries. The proposal's failure modes are (a) it sketches types that already exist under other names, (b) three places where a projection would manufacture precision the artifact does not contain, and (c) an engineering stack sized for a corpus browser when the first three slices need a single-story static artifact. Findings, numbered, with a recommendation each.

ARCHITECTURE / BOUNDARY
A1 Name collision. core.SurfaceAtlas is already 'the atlas' (exact evidence coordinate system, §21/§106). 'Narrative Atlas' as the product name is defensible — it is the surface atlas made navigable — but no scene type may be called Atlas. Recommend: portable module `scene` inside storymodel4s owning (ViewSpec, ProjectionContract, NarrativeScene, marks, visual laws), because those types must evolve in lockstep with StoryModel and the laws belong beside the artifact laws; the browser application is a separate workspace repo `storyatlas4s` consuming storymodel4s by git-SHA ProjectRef per workspace policy. Dependency direction storymodel4s -> storyatlas4s is forbidden.
A2 The seam is codec, which is empty. A browser client has no wire format; the scene compiler in the browser needs a serialized StoryModel[Validated] + FeatureTrack sidecars + HsmmResult. codec (M1 W6 item 14) is therefore the first Atlas deliverable, not a late one. Recommend the codec round-trip laws include 'scene(decode(encode(m)), v) == scene(m, v)'.
A3 Third read contract. story.AlignmentSource and align.SourceView already duplicate RelationLayer and ParticipantSummary. Do not add a third (a viz consumer) on top; unify into one read API that also carries §115's story.covering/supporting/worldTimeTransition/boundaryEvidence and features.values/aggregate/windowed — none of which exist. The Atlas's 'select text -> every supported claim' is exactly story.covering(span); build it once.
A4 Addressing. There is no stable address for a node/edge/span/claim: Violation.path, acquire.TargetRef(kind, id: String) and the proposal's PickId are three stringly-typed approximations. Recommend one ADT (name: NarrativeRef, in core or story): SurfaceUnit(id) | Tokens(TokenRange) | Span(SpanSet) | Situation | Segment | Entity | Context | Claim | Evidence | RecallUnit | AlignCell(unit, AlignState) | FeatureObs(space, FeatureTarget) | Edge(layer, from, to, context?). Three consumers benefit immediately (CLI inspect, critic findings, validator paths); VisualIdentity.narrativeRef is then a field, not a new scheme.
A5 Compiler precondition. The compiler must accept StoryModel[Validated] (or Adjudicated) only; Draft renders only under explicit draft chrome. NarrativeScene[S <: SceneStatus] should mirror ModelStatus rather than invent a parallel lattice.

WHERE A PROJECTION WOULD MANUFACTURE PRECISION
P1 Chronology Loom x_W = t_W(v) does not exist in the artifact. World time is TemporalEdge (Allen relations, canonical forms only) scoped per ContextId; the Hasse cover is computed ad hoc in align/bridge/StorySourceView and exposed only as SparseRelation. A total x coordinate is a linear extension, i.e. a layout choice; §23 and §113 say so explicitly. Recommend: (i) promote the poset (Hasse cover + Allen intervals) to a reusable story type; (ii) the Loom is a layered DAG layout: rank = longest path in the cover, Overlaps/During drawn as intervals, WorldTimeTransition.Unresolved(alternatives) drawn as a fan across the alternative ranks, incomparable events placed by discourse order with the legend stating 'x order among incomparable events is layout, not data'; (iii) per-context: the narrated-world context is the primary loom, Speech/Belief/Memory contexts are insets anchored to their holder situation — the announced battle, the battle, and the recounting in WOG live in three contexts and must not share one axis. Law: Before(a,b) => rank(a) < rank(b); no converse.
P2 Discourse Atlas x = center(sourceSupport). SpanSet is discontinuous by design (recurrence, motif, retold event). The center of a discontinuous support can fall on text that does not support the unit — violating the evidence law in the same section. Recommend: anchor = NarrativeGraph.discoursePosition (first span); every further span becomes a portal typed by NarrativeReference (Anaphoric/Retrospective/Summary/Partial/Thematic) — the vocabulary already exists in ReferenceEdge. Containment should be a hard constraint by construction (a segment's region is the hull of its children's regions at the finer level), so drop lambda_contain from the objective.
P3 Semantic zoom conflates two hierarchies. SegmentNode(level 3/2/1) + SituationNode is the narrative hierarchy; SurfaceUnitKind Paragraph/Sentence/Clause/Token is the surface hierarchy; PropositionChart bridges via document.ProjectionIndex. A single linear NarrativeScale forbids 'scene zoom with sentence text visible'. Recommend ZoomLevel = (narrativeLevel, surfaceDetail) with a monotone default path; state LOD laws per axis. Also: HierarchyKind has PrimarySegmentation plus auxiliary GoalArc/EntityThread/LocationThread/Theme. Territories are PrimarySegmentation only; the proposal's 'thread' is precisely auxiliary containment (possibly discontinuous) — a good fit, say so in the contract so nobody re-derives threads from mentions.

EPISTEMIC PLAYHEAD
E1 S_<=t = {c : evidenceEnd(c) <= t} is too weak. Evidence.upstream: Set[ClaimId] means the horizon is the transitive closure over ClaimLedger; a claim is visible at t iff all evidence in its closure ends <= t. Further consequences the ADR must state: (i) Resolved.alternatives at t may differ from omniscient alternatives — reader mode shows the t-restricted set; (ii) entity identity is time-indexed: CorefPartition restricted to mentions <= t is a coarser quotient, so 'the warriors' and 'ghosts' are distinct entities until the merging mention; (iii) windows crossing t are SurfaceWindow.complete = false (EdgePolicy exists) and must render as partial, not as a value; (iv) BoundaryBelief at the gap immediately before t needs right context and renders as 'not yet assessable', not low. Retrospective reinterpretation is a second ClaimMeta with a later evidence set, never a mutation — the append-only ledger already enforces this; the Atlas should render both statuses side by side at the earlier region.

UNCERTAINTY AND STYLE
U1 'Fog or hatching' collapses five distinct typed states: Estimate.Missing(reason), Credence with calibrated = None (raw), calibrated Probability, Resolved.alternatives / ResolutionState.Alternatives, ResolutionState.Unresolved, plus align Exclusion. Recommend styling laws: raw scores never share a visual scale with probabilities (raw -> ordinal ramp with a 'raw' marker; probability -> opacity/width); Missing is a distinct mark (never zero, never faded); Alternatives are a fan/split; Unresolved is an explicit placeholder mark. EpistemicStatus has six values (SurfaceExplicit, LinguisticallyEntailed, WorldKnowledgeInferred, StructurallyDerived, Hypothesized, HumanAdjudicated), not the proposal's four; use the six and require a non-colour channel for status.
U2 Add a law 'every scene has a textual twin': deterministic NarrativeScene -> text (Renderer.text already exists for models). It gives screen-reader access, snapshot diffs across model versions, and JVM-only testing of the compiler without a renderer.

RECALL VOYAGE
R1 The visual vocabulary must be generated from the alignment's state space, not written by hand. AlignState = Source(ref) | External(state) with ExternalState = Association | Commentary | SourceConsistentInference | Intrusion | Uninterpretable | Unranked. The proposal's omission/blending/gist/backtracking/elaboration are derived quantities: omission = AlignmentMatrix.columnMass below threshold; gist = mass on a Segment ref (massAtLevel); blending = multimodal AlignmentRow (topK); backtracking = backward transitions in TransitionFlow / RecallSignature.backwardMass; elaboration = recall-side ElaborationEdge. Recommend the ADR table ribbon width = row source mass, sharpness = localizability(K), branching = topK with mass above tau, off-map = six typed provinces, one per ExternalState (Unranked must not look like Intrusion). Population view aggregates AlignmentMatrix.visitation. Law: no visual category without a type in align.

FEATURE TOPOGRAPHY / SCALE-SPACE
F1 F(x,s) already exists as Windowed + ScalarReducer.Kernel(shape) + Coverage. Define FeatureWindowQuery as a FeatureDerivation plus a Ranking, so every scale-space row has a derivationId (content-addressed cache, receipts, stale-descendant detection for free). WindowBasis needs an Events basis (aggregate over FeatureTarget.Situation SpanSet) for the 'scale in events' axis.
F2 Circularity badge. A feature terrain drawn against boundaries must show whether that FeatureSpace appears in FeatureUseLedger with UsePurpose.Induction for those boundaries; CircularityCheck already computes it. Mission commitment 11 makes this mandatory, not optional.

ENGINEERING SCALE
S1 Tile pyramid is premature for slices 1–3. x is source order and LOD is the hierarchy, so the Discourse Atlas index is one-dimensional: (projection, level, tokenRange). Two-dimensional tiles are only needed for StoryWorld/LocalSemantic and for population recall. Every module is CrossType.Pure, so the scene compiler runs in the browser; static-artifact mode = serialized model + compiler in-page, no tile server until corpora. Defer tiles to slice 4.
S2 SVG first, from the same scene graph: publication figures, deterministic snapshot tests, and the DOM text rail come for free. Adopt a GPU backend only after a benchmark on a novel-length model shows the SVG backend cannot hold the mark budget at 60 fps. A deck.gl facade is a maintenance liability to be earned, not assumed.
S3 Determinism law: layout is a pure function of (artifact contentChecksum, ViewSpec). This excludes ELK/MSAGL unless seeded and version-pinned, and any JS-only layout breaks 'testable on the JVM'. Keep layouts in the portable module: Sugiyama for the Loom and causal backbone, StoryFlow-style thread layout for the Discourse Atlas.

SEQUENCING
Q1 Slice 1 (textual observatory) is buildable now against core + features + the WOG fixture and needs no story induction. Propose it as the HTML output of the M1 W6 `inspect` CLI, gated on codec. Slices 2–3 wait for M2 hierarchy induction — rendering hand fixtures as if they were built models would overclaim, exactly what the mission forbids. Do not start any GPU work before an automatically built StoryModel exists. The user study in §15 is a paper; keep the structural checks and performance gates, defer the study.

DECISIONS I AM ASKING YOU TO TAKE A POSITION ON: (1) A1 module split; (2) A4 NarrativeRef as an M1 item shared by inspect/critic/validator; (3) P1 Loom as poset layout with per-context insets; (4) R1 recall vocabulary generated from AlignState; (5) S2 SVG-first; (6) Q1 slice 1 = inspect HTML. Post your own findings too, especially where you think I am wrong about scope; I will fold agreed dispositions into rev 1 and draft ADR 0002 from it.
